title: Earth day colour, July 2004 (Blue Marble NG, topography + bathymetry shading), 8K
zh: 白天地球真彩色底图（NASA Blue Marble 下一代，2004年7月月合成，含陆地地形与海底地形阴影），8K
license: Public Domain (NASA imagery, not copyrighted in the US; NASA Media Usage Guidelines https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/)
author: Reto Stöckli, NASA Earth Observatory (NASA GSFC); Terra/MODIS data
credit_line: NASA Earth Observatory / Reto Stöckli (Blue Marble: Next Generation, NASA GSFC)
notes: Product: Blue Marble: Next Generation w/ Topography and Bathymetry, July 2004, file world.topo.bathy.200407.3x21600x10800.jpg (21600x10800, 2 km/px) -> DCT-halved then Lanczos-resampled to 8192x4096, JPEG q95 4:4:4 progressive. Cloud-free, northern-summer (green Northern Hemisphere, snow-free except high mountains/Greenland/Antarctica). Ocean colour is depth-shaded from bathymetry (light-blue continental shelves). Use as MeshStandardMaterial.map (sRGB). Equirectangular (plate carree), WGS84 lat/lon; left edge = 180°W, centre = 0° (Greenwich), top = 90°N; drops straight onto three.js SphereGeometry UVs (u=0 at 180°W). Pixel-aligned with every other earth_* map in this folder (verified with overlays).

title: Global cloud cover (Blue Marble: Clouds), 8K
zh: 全球云层（NASA 蓝色弹珠云图，白云黑底，可作云层球的 alpha/透明度贴图），8K
source_url: https://visibleearth.nasa.gov/images/57747/blue-marble-clouds (Visible Earth record now redirects to https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/ ; file still served by eoimages)
license: Public Domain (NASA imagery, not copyrighted in the US; NASA Media Usage Guidelines https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/)
author: Reto Stöckli (NASA GSFC), enhancements Robert Simmon; Terra/MODIS
credit_line: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center image by Reto Stöckli (clouds); enhancements by Robert Simmon (Blue Marble, Terra/MODIS data)
notes: Product: Blue Marble: Clouds (Visible Earth record 57747, published 2002-02-11), file cloud_combined_8192.tif (8192x4096, R=G=B verified) -> 8-bit grayscale JPEG q90 at native size. Composite of two days of MODIS visible imagery plus a third day of thermal IR over the poles. White clouds on black; median value 59, clear sky ~0-12. Antarctica and part of Greenland read bright (ice/cloud) — harmless because those are white in the day map. Minor streaking in the top ~10 rows at the North Pole (source artifact). Use as alphaMap/opacity on a slightly larger cloud sphere; a smoothstep(0.05,0.9) levels curve gives crisper clouds. Equirectangular (plate carree), WGS84 lat/lon; left edge = 180°W, centre = 0° (Greenwich), top = 90°N; drops straight onto three.js SphereGeometry UVs (u=0 at 180°W). Pixel-aligned with every other earth_* map in this folder (verified with overlays).

title: Land/water mask (white = water), derived, 4K
zh: 海陆掩膜（白=水体，黑=陆地/冰），用于海面高光/粗糙度，4K
license: Public Domain (NASA imagery, not copyrighted in the US; NASA Media Usage Guidelines https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/) (derived work by this project)
author: Derived by this project from NASA Blue Marble NG (Reto Stöckli) and NASA EO GEBCO bathymetry (Jesse Allen / GEBCO, BODC)
credit_line: NASA Earth Observatory / Reto Stöckli (Blue Marble: Next Generation, NASA GSFC); Imagery by Jesse Allen, NASA Earth Observatory, using data from the General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans (GEBCO) produced by the British Oceanographic Data Centre
notes: DERIVED (no official BMNG water-mask raster is published any more; the 8-bit GEBCO maps alone are ambiguous on shallow shelves/lowlands). Classified at 10800x5400 from the July day map colour (ocean = B-R>30 & B-G>12; inland water = near-black or blue/teal lakes) OR GEBCO bathymetry deeper than ~150 m, excluding bright ice (min RGB>150 => ice shelves count as land), 3x3 median, then BOX-downsampled to 4096x2048 => anti-aliased 8-bit coastlines. Includes Caspian, Great Lakes, Baikal, Victoria/Tanganyika/Malawi, Titicaca, Tibetan lakes. Pixel-exact match to earth_day_* coastlines (it was made from them). Use as roughness/metalness mask: e.g. roughness = mix(0.9, 0.25, mask). Equirectangular (plate carree), WGS84 lat/lon; left edge = 180°W, centre = 0° (Greenwich), top = 90°N; drops straight onto three.js SphereGeometry UVs (u=0 at 180°W). Pixel-aligned with every other earth_* map in this folder (verified with overlays).

title: Topography + bathymetry height map (GEBCO via NASA EO), 16-bit, 4K
zh: 全球高程/海底深度高度图（16位灰度，陆地+海底），可作位移/凹凸或海底电缆章节的海床起伏，4K
license: Public Domain (NASA imagery, not copyrighted in the US; NASA Media Usage Guidelines https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/); underlying GEBCO_08 grid is free to use with attribution to GEBCO
author: Jesse Allen (NASA Earth Observatory); GEBCO / British Oceanographic Data Centre; combined by this project
credit_line: Imagery by Jesse Allen, NASA Earth Observatory, using data from the General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans (GEBCO) produced by the British Oceanographic Data Centre
notes: Products: NASA EO "Topography" (gebco_08_rev_elev_21600x10800.png, land 0..6400 m in 0..255) + "Bathymetry" (gebco_08_rev_bath_21600x10800.png, ocean -8000..0 m in 0..255, land=255). Combined linearly h = elev*6400/255 - (255-bath)*8000/255 metres, averaged to 4096x2048 in float, saved as 16-bit grayscale PNG: code = (h + 8000) / 14400 * 65535 (sea level = 36408/65535 = 0.5556; in a browser-decoded 8-bit texture sea level ~= 141.7/255). Range clipped by the source products: deepest = -8000 m (trenches saturate), highest = +6400 m (Everest reads ~6036 m at 4K). Sanity samples: Tibet 4668 m, Dome A 4091 m, mid-Atlantic -2531 m. Equirectangular (plate carree), WGS84 lat/lon; left edge = 180°W, centre = 0° (Greenwich), top = 90°N; drops straight onto three.js SphereGeometry UVs (u=0 at 180°W). Pixel-aligned with every other earth_* map in this folder (verified with overlays).

title: Land relief tangent-space normal map (oceans flat), 4K
zh: 陆地地形法线贴图（海面保持平整，适合写实地球），4K
license: Public Domain (NASA imagery, not copyrighted in the US; NASA Media Usage Guidelines https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/) (derived work by this project)
author: Computed by this project from NASA EO / GEBCO topography
credit_line: Imagery by Jesse Allen, NASA Earth Observatory, using data from the General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans (GEBCO) produced by the British Oceanographic Data Centre
notes: Computed with pure Python from earth_height_4k data, land only (h<0 clamped to 0 so the sea surface is flat). Central differences on the sphere (dx = 2πR·cos(lat)/W with cos clamped >=0.1 near the poles, dy = πR/H, wraps across the dateline seamlessly), vertical exaggeration x10, encoded RGB = n*0.5+0.5. Tangent-space, OpenGL / three.js convention: +R = east (+u), +G = north (+v, image top), +B = up. Load with colorSpace = NoColorSpace (linear). Tune strength with material.normalScale (e.g. 0.5–2). Equirectangular (plate carree), WGS84 lat/lon; left edge = 180°W, centre = 0° (Greenwich), top = 90°N; drops straight onto three.js SphereGeometry UVs (u=0 at 180°W). Pixel-aligned with every other earth_* map in this folder (verified with overlays).

title: Deep Star Map 2020 (celestial coordinates), tone-mapped, 8K
zh: 全天星空背景（NASA SVS 深空星图 2020，基于 Gaia DR2 等 17 亿颗恒星，赤道坐标系），8K
license: NASA SVS: Public Domain (NASA Media Usage Guidelines) with credit requested; incorporates ESA Gaia DR2 + Hipparcos/Tycho-2 catalogue data — credit ESA/Gaia/DPAC (treat ESA-derived content as CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO: attribute, share-alike)
author: Ernie Wright (USRA) / NASA GSFC Scientific Visualization Studio; ESA/Gaia/DPAC (Gaia DR2), Hipparcos & Tycho-2
credit_line: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio (Deep Star Maps 2020, Ernie Wright/USRA). Gaia DR2: ESA/Gaia/DPAC
notes: Product: Deep Star Maps 2020, starmap_2020_8k.exr (OpenEXR half-float, ZIP, celestial ICRF/J2000 plate carree) decoded with a pure-Python EXR reader and tone-mapped 255*(0.7*v)^(1/2.2) (very close to SVS's own *_print.jpg look), JPEG q92 4:4:4 (no chroma subsampling so star colours survive). Orientation: Dec +90 at top; RA = 0h at the image CENTRE and RA increases to the LEFT (x = 0.5 - RA/24h, wrap) i.e. the sky as seen from inside the sphere — verified: Betelgeuse upper-left of Rigel, Antares at RA 16.5h/Dec -26°. Not Earth-aligned: for a background sphere viewed from inside, use side=BackSide and rotate to taste (or align to Earth by sidereal time). Milky Way, LMC/SMC visible.
